title: Russian Federation: Authorities impose censorship on media and crush peaceful anti-war protests following invasion of Ukraine
claim: Roskomnadzor ordered media to rely only on official Russian sources for invasion coverage and threatened sanctions for spreading false information, effectively imposing censorship.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights organization statement with specific legal and regulatory details.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s state apparatus because Roskomnadzor acted as the official media watchdog under his government.
contrary_evidence: Russian authorities framed the measure as preventing false information about the war.

title: Russia: Kremlin’s ruthless crackdown stifles independent journalism and anti-war movement
claim: Amnesty said Russian authorities blocked independent media, banned Facebook and Twitter, and had arbitrarily arrested more than 13,800 people at anti-war rallies since 24 February 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous NGO reporting with concrete arrest and censorship figures.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s government because the crackdown was implemented by state authorities and Roskomnadzor/police.
contrary_evidence: Authorities described the war and restrictions as necessary responses to the invasion and misinformation.

title: We publish a report on political prisoners and political repression in Russia in 2022
claim: Memorial said repression of public dissent reached unprecedented levels in 2022, political opposition was effectively outlawed, independent media were shut down, censorship was institutionalized, protest activity was suppressed, and the number of political prisoners reached 513 by the end of 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Major Russian rights project summarizing its own monitored casework and year-end counts.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s regime because the report describes state repression, censorship, and police-force conduct in 2022.
contrary_evidence: This is an advocacy-monitoring report and is retrospective rather than contemporaneous.

title: Политзаключённые и политические репрессии в России в 2022 году
claim: Memorial said 2022 was marked by de facto military censorship, 74 new names were added to the main political-prisoner list, and more than 5,000 administrative cases and 200-plus criminal cases targeted anti-army speech.
source_confidence_reason: Local-language retrospective report with explicit annual statistics and repression categories.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin’s regime because the report describes state repression in response to anti-war speech and public dissent.
contrary_evidence: The report is a retrospective summary and not a contemporaneous government record.

title: Russian Rhetoric Ahead of Attack Against Ukraine: Deny, Deflect, Mislead
claim: Putin and Kremlin officials repeatedly denied that Russia planned to invade Ukraine while calling Russia peaceful and saying it would not attack anyone; the article says that denial was proven false by the full-scale invasion on February 24.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous fact-check with direct quotations and immediate outcome confirmation.
ruler_attribution: Strong direct attribution: it quotes Putin and his spokesman as the speakers of the false denial campaign.
contrary_evidence: The Kremlin and Russian officials made the denials at the time.

title: Vladimir Putin repeats false claim of genocide in Ukraine
claim: PolitiFact says Putin repeated a false genocide claim in his February 24 address, and that there is no evidence supporting the claim that ethnic Russians in Ukraine faced genocide.
source_confidence_reason: Fact-check built around the president’s own speech and corroborating international evidence.
ruler_attribution: Strong direct attribution: the false claim is Putin’s own public justification for war.
contrary_evidence: Putin and Russian officials have long repeated the genocide allegation.

title: Vladimir Putin's false war claims
claim: DW says Putin’s stated reasons for war - including denazifying Ukraine and acting in self-defense - were false propaganda claims with no basis.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous fact-check with direct quotation of the speech and specific falsity determinations.
ruler_attribution: Strong direct attribution: Putin personally advanced the false justifications in a public address.

title: Putin's False Claim of Self-Defense While Starting a War on Ukraine
claim: VOA quotes Putin saying he launched a special military operation to protect people from genocide and to demilitarize Ukraine, then labels the self-defense claim false because no one attacked Russia.
source_confidence_reason: It reproduces Putin’s own statement and immediately evaluates it against the Charter and the facts on the ground.
ruler_attribution: Strong direct attribution: this is Putin’s own war justification, rebutted in the same item.
contrary_evidence: Putin’s statement itself framed the invasion as self-defense.

title: Russia's attack on Ukraine came after months of denials it would attack
claim: The Post reports that Russian officials spent weeks denying plans to attack Ukraine, ridiculing warnings as hysteria and fairy tales, before the full-scale assault began.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report summarizing a broad denial campaign immediately contradicted by events.
ruler_attribution: Strong direct attribution to Putin’s governing line, though the article notes some uncertainty about whether the denials were deliberate disinformation or closed decision-making.
contrary_evidence: The article notes it is not clear whether the denials were deliberate disinformation or closed-off decision-making.

title: World Court: Ukraine has filed suit against Russia, citing false genocide claims
claim: Reuters reports that the International Court of Justice confirmed Ukraine’s case and said Russia’s claim that it invaded to prevent genocide is false.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters summary of an ICJ filing and the court’s confirmation; strong corroboration, though still mediated reporting.
ruler_attribution: Strong indirect attribution: the false genocide rationale is Putin’s and Russia’s public justification for the invasion.
contrary_evidence: Russia publicly maintained the genocide justification.

title: Putin tells Russian business people he had no choice over Ukraine
claim: Putin told business leaders he had no other option but to order the operation against Ukraine and said Moscow had been forced into action.
source_confidence_reason: Direct Reuters report on a televised meeting and Putin’s own words.
ruler_attribution: Strong direct attribution: these are Putin’s own public statements explaining the invasion.

title: Why the U.S. is targeting Putin's daughters Katerina and Maria
claim: Reuters reports that U.S. officials believed Putin’s adult daughters were hiding his wealth, and that Maria Vorontsova led government-funded programs personally overseen by Putin.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters quotes U.S. officials and ties the family to state-funded programs; the wealth claim is still inferential rather than admitted.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the report ties concealment and benefits to Putin’s daughters and explicitly says officials believed the wealth was hidden with family members.
contrary_evidence: The Kremlin said it was bewildered by the sanctions and denied hidden family assets.

title: UK sanctions target the lavish lifestyles of Putin’s daughters
claim: The UK government said it sanctioned Putin’s daughters, described the Kremlin inner circle’s lavish lifestyles, and stated that more than £275 billion of Putin’s war chest had been frozen.
source_confidence_reason: Official sanctions notice with named designations and stated basis.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the action targets Putin’s family and the wider elite he governs.
contrary_evidence: The Kremlin rejected the broader sanctions framing.

title: U.S. Treasury Escalates Sanctions on Russia for Its Atrocities in Ukraine
claim: Treasury said it was targeting family members of President Vladimir Putin as part of sanctions imposed in response to Russia’s war against Ukraine.
source_confidence_reason: Official OFAC sanctions notice with explicit designation rationale.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the sanctions are expressly aimed at Putin’s family and war support network.

title: Treasury Sanctions Kremlin Elites, Leaders, Oligarchs, and Family for Enabling Putin’s War Against Ukraine
claim: Treasury said three of Putin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov’s family members lived lifestyles incongruous with his salary and likely built on ill-gotten wealth from his connections to Putin, including a property empire worth more than $10 million.
source_confidence_reason: Official sanctions notice with unusually specific descriptions of the family wealth and its purported source.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the claim is about Putin’s spokesperson and the personal network around Putin, not a direct Putin self-confession.
contrary_evidence: Peskov has publicly denied the asset claims in related reporting.

title: Russian Asset Tracker
claim: OCCRP said its final update documented more than $19.8 billion in assets owned by Russia’s rich and powerful and that the assets were tied through documentary evidence to Putin’s circle.
source_confidence_reason: Large investigative compilation based on documentary tracing; strong for the existence of a hidden-asset network, though not every item is equally direct.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: it explicitly ties the asset network to Putin’s circle rather than to Russia in the abstract.
contrary_evidence: Documentary tracing still does not prove every asset is personally owned by Putin.

title: Russian activists publish leaked photos of Putin-linked palace
claim: Leaked photographs confirmed details of a luxurious palace allegedly built for Putin’s personal use, including a marble pool, hookah lounge, wine cellar and theatre.
source_confidence_reason: Investigative reporting based on leaked photographs and prior anti-corruption work; the ownership claim remains alleged rather than admitted.
period_fit: Pre-2022 pattern evidence still relevant to the 2022 ruler-period because it concerns an active personal-wealth allegation around Putin.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the property is reported as Putin-linked and allegedly for his personal use, but the Kremlin denied ownership.
contrary_evidence: The Russian president denied that the residence was built for his personal use.

title: ICIJ’s guide to Russian wealth hidden offshore
claim: ICIJ said its reporting had revealed hidden financial networks of oligarchs, businesses, frontmen and professionals who backed Vladimir Putin’s rise to power, and that much of Russia’s ruling-elite wealth is hidden offshore.
source_confidence_reason: High-quality investigative summary grounded in prior ICIJ leaks and reporting, though it synthesizes rather than adjudicates ownership in each case.
period_fit: Pre-2022 pattern evidence relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the guide explicitly links the offshore networks to Putin’s rise and his inner circle.
contrary_evidence: ICIJ notes that presence in offshore leaks does not by itself prove illegality.

title: How a network of enablers have helped Russia’s oligarchs hide their wealth abroad
claim: ICIJ said elites close to Vladimir Putin funneled billions through tax havens to evade scrutiny and oversight, with lawyers, proxies and bankers making it possible.
source_confidence_reason: Investigative synthesis of offshore records and leak-based reporting, strong on pattern and network behavior.
period_fit: Pre-2022 pattern evidence relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the wealth-hiding network is explicitly described as being close to Putin.
contrary_evidence: The item describes network behavior; it is not a direct admission by Putin.

title: We Cannot Use It: Leaked E-Mails Show How Russian Petrochemical Giant Sibur Paid For Villa Linked to Putin
claim: OCCRP said leaked emails showed Sibur spent large sums on Villa Sellgren, a mansion on the Gulf of Finland reported as a Putin vacation destination, and that employees did not understand why the money was being spent.
source_confidence_reason: Document-backed investigative reporting with leaked emails and corroborating prior reporting.
period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year and tied to a long-running Putin-linked property pattern.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the property is reported as Putin-linked and the funding flowed through a company long associated with him and his family.
contrary_evidence: The company and associated actors did not publicly explain the spending as ordinary business necessity.

title: Putin's Friend Receives State Funding to Combat Corruption
claim: OCCRP reported that Arkady Rotenberg, a childhood friend of Putin, won a state contract for anti-corruption training, and that Putin had earlier created a state body that handed Rotenberg control over part of the vodka market.
source_confidence_reason: Older investigative reporting with concrete state-contract and ownership details that are directly relevant to patronage patterns.
period_fit: Pre-2022 pattern evidence relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the item concerns a childhood friend of Putin receiving state benefit through proximity to Putin.

title: Cars, Connections, and Contracts in Putin’s Russia
claim: OCCRP reported that companies with ties to Russia’s security and prosecutorial elite won large state contracts and that watchdogs described this as a common pattern where taxpayers’ money flows to those close to the elite.
source_confidence_reason: Documentary investigative reporting showing a recurring conflict-of-interest pattern in the Putin-era state.
period_fit: Pre-2022 pattern evidence relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the article situates the contract pattern inside the Putin-era elite network.

title: Leaked Emails Reveal How Putin’s Friends Dodged Sanctions With Help of Western Enablers
claim: OCCRP published leaked emails showing a memo labeled Objective: Clear Sanctions that described a restructuring plan to preserve the Rotenberg brothers’ share in Helsinki Halli.
source_confidence_reason: Direct documentary leak with explicit sanctions-evasion planning.
period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year, though the conduct is rooted in earlier sanctions circumvention.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the brothers are long-time Putin associates, and the concealment behavior is tied to Putin’s orbit.
contrary_evidence: The source relies on leaked emails and describes an alleged restructuring plan rather than a judicial finding.

title: Treasury Sanctions Russian Officials, Members Of The Russian Leadership’s Inner Circle, And An Entity For Involvement In The Situation In Ukraine
claim: Treasury said Putin has investments in Gunvor, that the Rotenberg brothers received about $7 billion in contracts awarded by Putin, and that Yuri Kovalchuk was Putin’s personal banker and cashiers-like advisor.
source_confidence_reason: Official sanctions notice with unusually explicit descriptions of the Putin inner circle’s financial and contract links.
period_fit: Pre-2022 pattern evidence relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the notice directly ties financial benefit, contracts and access to Putin’s personal circle.
contrary_evidence: This is a sanctions finding, not a criminal verdict; the government notice is itself an accusation-based instrument.

title: Russia: Fraud charges against Aleksei Navalny are arbitrary and politically motivated
claim: Amnesty concluded that the new fraud charges against Navalny were politically motivated and aimed to criminalize his anti-corruption and political activism.
source_confidence_reason: Direct human-rights assessment of a politically sensitive prosecution closely tied to anti-corruption scrutiny of the Putin system.
ruler_attribution: Strong indirect attribution: the prosecution targeted Navalny’s anti-corruption work against Putin-linked elites, but the item stops short of proving Putin personally ordered the charge.
contrary_evidence: The Russian authorities presented the case as a legal fraud prosecution.

title: Russia: One year after jailing, Aleksei Navalny and his associates in a living hell
claim: Amnesty said Russian authorities dismantled Navalny’s Anti-Corruption Foundation, labelled his organizations extremist, blocked their websites, and criminalized their activities.
source_confidence_reason: Direct human-rights reporting on state suppression of an anti-corruption movement with clear, traceable dates and actions.
period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year and immediately prior to the invasion period.
ruler_attribution: Strong indirect attribution: the crackdown targeted the leading anti-corruption network challenging Putin’s circle, but the item does not itself prove direct personal orders.

title: Navalnyy and Others v. Russia
claim: The court record notes that Navalny’s 2017 film alleged a high-ranking state official used charities and shell companies to amass luxuries, and that he brought an Article 18 political-ends complaint over his arrest and detention.
source_confidence_reason: Judicial record from the European Court, directly describing the anti-corruption allegation and the political-purpose complaint.
period_fit: Retrospective judicial evidence about a long-running pattern relevant to the 2022 ruler-period.
ruler_attribution: Strong indirect attribution: the case concerns anti-corruption allegations against a high-ranking state official within the Putin system and state treatment of the investigator.
contrary_evidence: The judgment addresses complaints and procedure; it is not a confession by Putin.
